page: OVHcloud t2-le-180 is a dedicated GPU-accelerated server instance within the Cloud GPU family. The system is provisioned on the KVM hypervisor with 60 dedicated x86_64 physical cores (60 vCPUs) powered by Intel Xeon 6226R processors running at a base clock speed of 2.9 GHz. It features 180 GB of system RAM, allocating 3.0 GB of memory per core. Compute acceleration is supplied by four NVIDIA Volta V100S GPUs providing a total pool of 128 GB VRAM (32 GB per GPU). Storage is handled locally by a 500 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by a 10 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark outcomes show high performance in GPU-driven machine learning workloads alongside balanced host CPU performance. The four V100S GPUs achieve top-tier throughput in prompt processing for both small 135M models (15,284.46 tokens/sec) and medium 7B models (1,277.99 tokens/sec), as well as text generation on medium models (120.29 tokens/sec). Host CPU execution performs in the average tier across stress-ng tests (1,476.79 single-core and 59,632.01 multi-core) and Geekbench suites (1,239.0 single-core, 10,938.0 multi-core). Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches top-quartile speeds at 311.42 GB/sec, and the PassMark memory benchmark reflects strong data handling with a score of 2,794.65.

The primary resource tradeoff centers on the balance between high-density GPU acceleration and relatively modest local storage, as the 500 GB NVMe SSD limits local dataset caching. By pairing 60 physical cores with four accelerator units and substantial VRAM, the t2-le-180 delivers high hardware density per host node. This profile is well suited for multi-GPU distributed deep learning training, AI inference serving for small to mid-sized language models, parallel scientific simulations, and GPU-accelerated video rendering pipelines.
description: OVHcloud t2-le-180 is a dedicated GPU-accelerated server powered by 60 physical cores of Intel Xeon 6226R processors clocked at 2.9 GHz, 180 GB of system RAM, and 500 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Acceleration is driven by four NVIDIA Volta V100S GPUs offering a collective 128 GB of VRAM. Supported by a 10 Gbps baseline network, the instance demonstrates top-tier benchmark efficiency in small and medium LLM inference tasks, generating up to 120.29 tokens per second on 7B models and reaching 15,284.46 prompt processing tokens per second on 135M architectures. CPU multi-threaded workloads show solid throughput, such as 311.42 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. The system is designed for distributed deep learning, multi-model AI inference, parallel batch compute, and high-throughput scientific simulations requiring multi-GPU setups.
